system_description.narrative_title: AI compute boom concentrates risk around chips, capital and infrastructure
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid, capital-intensive AI build-out is creating concentrated demand for a handful of chips and suppliers (notably Nvidia), triggering massive financing, supply-chain stress and new risk-management responses across markets, insurers and governments. The concentration is reshaping capital flows, corporate restructuring and energy/infrastructure needs while prompting regulatory, geopolitical and labor reactions as states and investors scramble to contain systemic and security risks.
system_description.scope: The commercial AI-industrial ecosystem: hyperscalers, chipmakers and OEMs, AI model developers and startups, financial markets and lenders, insurers, energy and supply-chain infrastructure, and national regulators/policy responses directly engaged in enabling or constraining large-scale AI deployment.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic-technology system (global economy, geopolitics and critical infrastructure)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets, banking and corporate credit
National security and trade policy (tech competition, export controls)
Labor markets and social policy (workforce displacement and reskilling)
evidence_headlines: SpaceX looks to raise $40bn to buy Nvidia chips in financing led by Apollo
Nvidia turns to insurers to spread the risk of AI build-out
World Bank warns of AI concentration risks as it lifts East Asia and Pacific growth outlook to 4.5%
US power use to beat record highs in 2026 and 2027 as AI use surges, EIA says
Investors look to shelter portfolios from rising AI concentration risks
Norway's biggest bank DNB to lay off around 400 staff amid AI-driven changes

variables.name: Compute demand concentration
variables.description: Degree to which aggregate AI compute demand is concentrated on a small subset of hardware types and supplier channels.

variables.name: Capital flow to AI
variables.description: Rate of new investment and financing directed toward AI compute, infrastructure and model development.

variables.name: Specialized chip supply capacity
variables.description: Available production capacity of chips and accelerators designed specifically for large-scale AI workloads.

variables.name: Supplier market concentration
variables.description: Degree of market share concentration among suppliers of critical AI hardware, software stacks and components.

variables.name: Financial leverage exposure
variables.description: Aggregate level of leverage and debt financing that is directly tied to AI infrastructure and procurement commitments.

variables.name: Energy use rate for AI
variables.description: Current rate of electricity consumption attributable to AI training, inference and associated infrastructure.

variables.name: Power grid capacity margin
variables.description: Available spare electrical generation and transmission capacity relative to peak demand including AI loads.

variables.name: Data center infrastructure capacity
variables.description: Aggregate usable compute, cooling and networking capacity in data centers relevant to AI workloads.

variables.name: Supply chain stress level
variables.description: Degree of disruption, lead-time variability and bottlenecks across the supply chain for AI components and materials.

variables.name: Insurance exposure to AI
variables.description: Accumulated insured or underwritten financial exposure and claims potential linked to AI-related losses and liabilities.

variables.name: Regulatory activity intensity
variables.description: Level and pace of policy-making, regulatory interventions and compliance requirements targeting large-scale AI deployment.

variables.name: Geopolitical technology fragmentation pressure
variables.description: Degree of political and trade pressure causing fragmentation or decoupling of technology supply chains and standards.

variables.name: Labor displacement and restructuring rate
variables.description: Rate at which employment roles are automated, restructured or displaced due to AI deployment across sectors.

variables.name: Model development activity
variables.description: Rate and scale of development, training and deployment of large AI models and agentic systems.

variables.name: Market valuation concentration
variables.description: Extent to which equity market capitalization and investor returns are concentrated in a small set of AI-exposed entities.

variables.name: Systemic security externalities
variables.description: Aggregate level of security risks, misuse potential and negative spillovers from widespread AI capability deployment.

catalysts.title: SpaceX seeks $40bn to buy Nvidia GPUs
catalysts.description: Ongoing financing talks to raise roughly $40 billion to purchase Nvidia GPUs for AI capacity expansion; deal structure and scale could rapidly shift demand and leverage dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'SpaceX looks to raise $40bn to buy Nvidia chips'; 'SpaceX seeks to raise $40 bln to buy Nvidia chips'; 'Apollo, banks in talks to finance SpaceX's $40 billion Nvidia GPU purchase'.

catalysts.title: AMD plans substantial supply increase in 2027
catalysts.description: AMD's announced plan to materially ramp supply in 2027 will expand non-Nvidia accelerator availability and alter supplier concentration and lead times.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'AMD plans to substantially increase supply in 2027, CEO says.'

catalysts.title: Surging US power use to beat records in 2026–27
catalysts.description: EIA forecasts record-high US electricity consumption driven in part by AI workloads, stressing grids and driving energy-related planning and investments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US power use to beat record highs in 2026 and 2027 as AI use surges, EIA says.'

catalysts.title: Record debt financings to buy AI chips
catalysts.description: Banks and corporates are structuring blockbuster debt packages to fund chip purchases and AI infrastructure, concentrating capital flows and on‑balance-sheet leverage.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Wall Street banks launch record $60bn chip deal for Broadcom and Anthropic'; 'Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX Seek Blockbuster Debt Deals to Pay for AI Chips.'

catalysts.title: Nvidia seeks insurers to spread AI build-out risk
catalysts.description: Nvidia's move to transfer build‑out risks to insurers will expand insured exposure and influence how systemic supplier risks are underwritten.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nvidia turns to insurers to spread the risk of AI build-out.'

catalysts.title: South Korea to develop $3.5bn frontier AI model starting next year
catalysts.description: A government-led $3.5 billion frontier AI model program will boost national model development and require significant compute and capital.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'South Korea plans to develop $3.5 billion frontier AI model starting next year.'

catalysts.title: Japan Rapidus $15bn chip bet outcome
catalysts.description: The success or failure of Rapidus securing customers for its $15 billion chip investment will determine additional regional specialized capacity and supplier competition.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Japan's $15 billion Rapidus chip bet hinges on winning customers.'

catalysts.title: AMD explores foundry partnership with Samsung
catalysts.description: Ongoing exploration of a foundry tie-up between AMD and Samsung could increase fabrication capacity for AI chips and shift supplier dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'AMD CEO says continues to explore foundry partnership with Samsung Electronics.'

catalysts.title: Investors shelter portfolios from AI concentration risks
catalysts.description: Asset managers and pension funds shifting allocations away from highly concentrated AI winners could redistribute capital and pressure valuations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Investors look to shelter portfolios from rising AI concentration risks'; 'Global pension funds cut US equities over AI concentration risk.'
